source.display_title: 05/27/2026 - IMRAN RAFI x Harry Edmonds — Follow Up

rep.name: Harry Edmonds
rep.location: Currently in Birmingham, UK; normally London and spends time in Thailand

prospect.name: Imran Rafi
prospect.location: Spain (city not stated); originally from England, left about eight years ago
prospect.occupation: Restaurateur — owns three independent hospitality businesses (a cafe, an Asian street food place and a recently opened Middle Eastern restaurant), one a limited company and two sole trader; leads 25 staff
prospect.family_status: Partner who is into fitness and has been pregnant for much of the last two years; three children, including young toddlers at home and one who lives elsewhere
prospect.training_background: Played a lot of rugby as a teenager. Four to five years of on-and-off kettlebell training on his terrace, self-programmed from Trevor's and other creators' YouTube clips — four or five movements for 15 minutes. Cycles of keto and fasting on and off for eight years, currently three weeks into a keto/20-hour-fast block. Had a personal trainer for a year (a gift from his partner) with results he judged negligible. Previously signed up to online platforms including GMB (Gold Medal Bodies). Can do 25-30 minutes of halos but describes his press-ups as rubbish and cannot pull himself up a rope.
prospect.medical: Nothing disclosed. Has blood checks, describes himself as fine and still agile. Was 87 kg, now 80 kg, about 4 kg from his target; earlier described himself as around 10 kg overweight. States 'I can't afford an injury at this age' but reports no current injury or condition.

signals: Explicitly capable of doing it alone and has: 'I could 100% do it on my own. I have done it on my own before.'
Paid coaching has already failed him once — a year of personal training produced 'very little change' and 'I actually got a lot more done when I was by myself'
Anchored roughly 4x below the offer: 'I thought it was going to be like, you know, 200 euros a month, or 300 euros a month'
Prices the offer against his level of need rather than his ability to pay: 'if that's the price I'm paying for just discipline, then it's steep. If it's complete and help me, dying, then I'll pay it'

goals.text: Lose the last four kilos and get properly shredded rather than just lighter
Round off his shoulders and build his back — fix the specifically weak parts of his game
Be able to climb a rope a couple of metres, a promise he has made himself for three years
Build discipline and structure so it stops being a three-week burst followed by falling off
Create a culture of fitness in the home for his toddlers by training at home rather than at a gym
Look and feel consistent with the energetic 25-year-old he feels like inside, and with leading a young team of 25
Confidence in the movements so he does not get injured — 'I can't afford an injury at this age'
Be strong for the next 25 years
Hit the deal he made with himself before he turns 50 in November

pains.text: Three-week bursts followed by falling off the wagon whenever work intervenes — 'I'll stay off the wagon for a while, and I'll just get fat'
Runs three restaurants and is constantly tasting food, which breaks the keto block
All-or-nothing personality — one taste and 'I've broken it, so it for the rest of the day'
A year of paid personal training produced almost nothing and cost him faith in coaching
No confidence in his kettlebell form and nobody to correct it
Three years of failing a promise he made to himself, which he describes as deflating
Body does not match his self-image — 'I feel like I'm a 25-year-old still inside. When I see the body, I'm like, nah, dude, what are you doing?'
Opened three businesses in four years, which consumed everything else

objections.raw_quote: That's a lot more than I was thinking... I thought it was going to be like, you know, 200 euros a month, or 300 euros a month, that's a grand a month, dude, that's so steep
objections.rep_response: Asked 'Is it worth it? Is the outcome worth it?', reframed the number as commitment ('it gives you 5,160 reasons to stick to it'), offered to structure the invoice for a tax write-off, then presented a three-month tier and a one-month trial

objections.raw_quote: I could 100% do it on my own. I have done it on my own before.
objections.rep_response: Named it directly and challenged it later: 'let go of like the pride element of I can do it on my own and just go and achieve your goal in six months'

objections.raw_quote: I really have to look at those numbers and think about it really carefully
objections.rep_response: Accepted it, exchanged WhatsApp numbers and messaged him live on the call so he had the contact; no follow-up call booked

objections.raw_quote: I go to a wedding in in Corsica in a couple in a week in about 10 days time i'll be there for three weeks
objections.rep_response: Agreed that it was poor timing rather than working it — 'you're not giving it 100% if you're on holiday, you just can't, you can maintain a little bit... it's up to you, man'

offer.payment_plan_terms: No instalments discussed. The one-month trial was offered as the way to reduce the up-front commitment: 'at the end of that month, you can continue. There's not going to be an extra. You just pay the balance of whichever one you wanted to do.'
offer.guarantee_mentioned: 'From your starting weight, you will be doing all those movements with the same volume intensity with 20 pounds heavier, about eight kilo... you'll double your strength in the six months, guaranteed, or we'll work with you until you are at the double.'

prospect_financials.notes: Volunteered that he can afford more than he used to — 'It's not a chef's wage anymore' — but framed EUR 1,000/month as roughly 20% of his monthly outgoings with three children. Money in his Spanish limited company cannot be extracted without a further 25% personal tax on top of 25% corporate tax, which is why the write-off framing appealed.

evidence: No decision and no payment: 'Give me a couple of days to think about it'
Explicitly rejected the six-month tier: 'I don't think it will be the six months to buy it off, because it's too much of an investment for me straight off the bat'
Live intent on the smaller tiers: 'I'm looking more at the one month, maybe even the three months'
WhatsApp numbers exchanged and a message sent during the call, so a channel exists
Counter-evidence: he leaves for a three-week trip in about ten days and both parties agreed that was a bad moment to start, with no follow-up call booked
outcome.next_step: Prospect to think for a couple of days and contact the rep on WhatsApp; leaning toward the one-month trial or the three-month tier

notable.note: The clearest discount ladder in the batch: on price hesitation the offer moved from EUR 5,160 for six months to EUR 3,400 for three months to a EUR 1,030 one-month 'love it or leave it' trial inside about five minutes, none of which exists in the stated $6,000/$9,000 offer. The rep also opened by describing his role as 'I just handle the onboard and stuff' and only disclosed he was hired as a closer at minute 27, and offered to frame the invoice so a personal coaching fee could be run through the prospect's Spanish limited company. This is the most ICP-core prospect in the batch and the one who received the deepest discounting.

quality.notes: Attribution inverts frequently — the rep's open question at 00:00:52, the entire three-month and one-month pricing exchange around 00:24:02 and the holiday discussion at 00:30:12 sit under the wrong labels, and several rep lines appear mid-block inside prospect turns. The pricing sequence in particular required reconstruction from content; the figures themselves are unambiguous.
